title: android:debuggable="true" set explicitly on <application>
sink: JDWP debugger attach / `adb shell run-as <pkg>` shell access to the app sandbox
sanitizer_notes: No evidence of a release-variant build flag or manifest-merger override stripping this attribute; it is set as a literal, unconditional value in the manifest under audit.

evidence.detail: AndroidManifest.xml <application> tag: android:name=".VulnBankApp" android:allowBackup="true" android:debuggable="true" android:label="VulnBank Demo" ... (lines 7-13 of extracted/AndroidManifest.xml)

reproduction_static: 1. Open the decoded AndroidManifest.xml. 2. Confirm android:debuggable="true" is present on the <application> element (not a tool-injected default -- apktool/aapt only emit this when it is actually set, e.g. via a debug build variant or explicit manifest entry). 3. Cross-check against any available build.gradle (none exists for this fixture) to see which build type set it.
reproduction_dynamic: If an installable build matching this manifest becomes available, confirm with `adb shell run-as com.vulnbankdemo.app id` (succeeds without root if debuggable) and/or jdb/`adb shell am attach-debugger` against the forwarded JDWP port -- suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier per MAN-18. No APK/installable package exists for this fixture today, so this cannot be executed now.
notes: target-profile.md flags this as explicitly set (not a decompiler artifact). If this manifest reflects a genuinely shipped release build, debuggable=true permits debugger attachment and run-as shell access, undermining every other control; if it is actually a non-release/test build, the finding stands against *this* build specifically. This is a hand-authored fixture manifest (no APK/source exists) -- treat confidence accordingly, but the declaration itself is the audit target, not an extraction artifact.

title: android:allowBackup="true" with no backup-content restriction on a banking app
source: android:allowBackup="true" on <application>; no android:fullBackupContent; no android:dataExtractionRules
sink: `adb backup`/cloud auto-backup extraction of the app's private data directory (SharedPreferences, SQLite DBs, files)
sanitizer_notes: No fullBackupContent XML or dataExtractionRules XML is referenced anywhere in the manifest to exclude sensitive files (e.g. session tokens, cached account data) from backup; no attribute narrows the default full-data backup.

evidence.detail: <application android:name=".VulnBankApp" android:allowBackup="true" android:debuggable="true" android:label="VulnBank Demo" ...> -- no fullBackupContent/dataExtractionRules attribute present anywhere in the file (lines 7-13).

reproduction_static: 1. Inspect <application> for the allowBackup value and absence of fullBackupContent/dataExtractionRules. 2. Confirm no backup_rules.xml/data_extraction_rules.xml is referenced anywhere in the manifest.
reproduction_dynamic: On a device with this app installed and USB debugging enabled: `adb backup -noapk com.vulnbankdemo.app` then inspect the resulting tarball for app_data contents -- suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier (MAN-18) once an installable build exists; not executable against this manifest-only fixture today.
notes: Given the app's apparent purpose (banking/money transfer, per .ui.TransferMoneyActivity and .data.AccountProvider class names), any session tokens or cached account data stored locally would be subject to backup extraction by anyone with physical/ADB access to an unlocked, debugging-enabled device. Severity would rise if storage-crypto-auditor confirms sensitive data is actually persisted unencrypted -- cross-reference that specialist's output when available.

title: TransferMoneyActivity exported with BROWSABLE custom-scheme deep link and no permission guard
source: Any installed app, or a web page/link opened in a mobile browser (category BROWSABLE), sending/navigating to an Intent with action=VIEW, data=vulnbank://transfer
sink: TransferMoneyActivity's Intent-handling code (onCreate/onNewIntent) -- implementation not present in this manifest-only artifact, but the class name strongly implies a money-movement action
sanitizer_notes: No android:permission attribute on the <activity>; no custom <permission> is defined anywhere in the manifest, so there is no signature-level gate even available to apply; no android:autoVerify / https App Link verification is used for this scheme (it is a bare custom scheme, not a verified App Link), so scheme-collision by another installed app is also possible in addition to direct exposure.
reproduction_static: 1. Locate <activity android:name=".ui.TransferMoneyActivity"> in the manifest. 2. Confirm android:exported="true" and the absence of android:permission. 3. Confirm the intent-filter carries BROWSABLE plus a custom scheme/host (vulnbank://transfer), making it reachable both from any other installed app via an explicit/implicit Intent and from a mobile browser via an intent:// or vulnbank:// link.
reproduction_dynamic: Suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier if a stub/installable APK is ever built from this manifest (none exists today, per target-profile.md): `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "vulnbank://transfer" com.vulnbankdemo.app` and, separately, host an HTML page with `<a href="vulnbank://transfer">` opened in a mobile browser, to confirm the activity launches without any prompt/permission check (MAN-18). Also worth a drozer `app.activity.start` / `app.activity.info` pass.
final_rating_reason: Reachability is unambiguous static proof (exported, BROWSABLE, no permission infrastructure anywhere in the manifest); both independent skeptics stand on that. But both also name a plausible, unresolved conditional neither could rule out: an in-app confirmation/auth step before a transfer actually executes, unverifiable because no implementation code exists for this fixture. Per severity-rating.md, a plausible unresolved conditional on static-only evidence caps this at Potential, not Confirmed.
notes: Exported-ness alone would not be a finding (deep-link entry activities are often intentionally public), but the combination of (a) a money-transfer-implying name, (b) zero permission guard, and (c) BROWSABLE web-reachability pushes attacker_model to 'remote' at minimum per the escalation rule (any webpage can fire an intent:// link). Hand off the actual Intent-extra parsing/validation question (does it require prior auth state, does it trust extras blindly, is there a confirmation screen) to android-ipc-ui-auditor and taint-flow-analyst; also cross-reference deeplink-clipboard-auditor's DLK-01..08 checks (clipboard-webview-oauth.md) and WEB-11 for the webpage-triggered angle. No implementation code exists in this fixture to confirm actual impact -- this finding is scoped to the manifest-level exposure only.

title: AccountProvider exported with no permission, no path-permission, no URI scoping
source: Any installed app issuing a ContentResolver query()/insert()/update()/delete() against content://com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider, no permission required
sink: AccountProvider's query/insert/update/delete implementation (not present in this manifest-only artifact); the class name implies it backs account/financial data
sanitizer_notes: No android:readPermission, android:writePermission, or android:permission attribute on the <provider>; no <path-permission> child elements to narrow exposure by sub-path; no android:grantUriPermissions scoping (moot here since the entire authority is already unrestricted); single flat authority with no path segmentation at all.

evidence.detail: <provider android:name=".data.AccountProvider" android:authorities="com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider" android:exported="true" /> (lines 35-38) -- no child elements, no permission attributes of any kind.

reproduction_static: 1. Locate <provider android:name=".data.AccountProvider"> in the manifest. 2. Confirm android:exported="true" with no android:readPermission/writePermission/permission attribute and no <path-permission> children. 3. Note the authority string for use in a content:// URI.
reproduction_dynamic: Suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier if an installable build is ever produced (none exists today): `adb shell content query --uri content://com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider` and the corresponding insert/update/delete variants, run from an unprivileged shell, to confirm what data is actually returned/mutated without holding any permission (MAN-18). Also check for SQL-injection-style selection/sortOrder parameter handling once implementation code is available.
notes: This is the second standout manifest-level fact per target-profile.md. Actual exploitability (data returned, whether raw SQL is used making it injectable, whether mutation is possible) depends entirely on AccountProvider's implementation, which does not exist in this fixture -- hand off to android-ipc-ui-auditor (advanced-attacks.md IPC checks) for that layer. The manifest-level fact alone (fully exported, zero access control, account-data-implying name) already clears the bar for a flagged finding per the 'export + apparent sensitive purpose' rule.

title: No <uses-sdk> declared -- min/targetSdkVersion undeclared in this manifest
sink: N/A -- this is a configuration gap, not a direct reachable sink; it changes which version-gated platform defaults apply (e.g. pre-API-17 default-exported-if-intent-filter, pre-API-28 cleartext-traffic-permitted default, pre-API-31 exported defaults, pre-API-33/34 notification/FGS requirements)
sanitizer_notes: No targetSdkVersion/minSdkVersion attribute is present anywhere in this manifest to confirm or rule out legacy insecure defaults. In this specific fixture the three declared components all set android:exported explicitly, so the API<17/31 default-exported ambiguity happens not to matter for them -- but any other version-gated default (cleartext traffic, backup policy nuances, etc.) cannot be resolved from this artifact.

evidence.detail: Full-text review of the manifest root <manifest> element and its direct children: no <uses-sdk android:minSdkVersion=... android:targetSdkVersion=.../> element exists anywhere in the file.

reproduction_static: 1. Search the manifest for <uses-sdk>. 2. Confirm no match. 3. Note that if this reflects a real build's merged manifest (not just this standalone fixture), the build system would normally have injected minSdkVersion/targetSdkVersion from build.gradle during the build -- their total absence here means either the source build.gradle itself never set them (defaulting minSdkVersion to 1), or this artifact is a hand-trimmed/synthetic manifest.
reproduction_dynamic: If an installable APK is ever produced, confirm the actual effective values with `aapt2 dump badging <apk>.apk` or `adb shell dumpsys package com.vulnbankdemo.app | grep -i sdk` -- suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier per MAN-18.
notes: target-profile.md independently flagged this same gap and cautioned downstream specialists against assuming a modern target SDK. Logged here as a formal MAN-12 finding per the audit checklist, but kept low severity/informational in character since this fixture is confirmed hand-authored (per target-profile.md and the fixture's own scope.md/README.md) rather than extracted from a real built APK -- the real-world risk only materializes if a genuinely shipped build also lacks these values, which would be unusual for a Play Store release (Play Console enforces a minimum targetSdkVersion) but is exactly the kind of thing worth re-checking against the actual build.gradle/merged manifest if this target is ever supplied as a full APK.

title: Exported component inventory for this manifest (IPC surface map for downstream specialists)
source: N/A -- inventory note, not an individual exploitable path
sink: N/A -- see AND-MAN-003 and AND-MAN-004 for the two components with apparent sensitive purpose
sanitizer_notes: LoginActivity is exported with only a MAIN/LAUNCHER intent-filter and no sensitive-sounding purpose -- exported-ness here is expected/required (it is the app's entry point) and is not itself a weakness. TransferMoneyActivity and AccountProvider are the two components with apparent sensitive purpose and no access control; see AND-MAN-003 and AND-MAN-004 respectively for the full analysis of those two.

evidence.detail: Complete <application> block contains exactly three components, no <service>/<receiver> elements at all: (1) <activity android:name=".ui.LoginActivity" android:exported="true"> with MAIN/LAUNCHER intent-filter; (2) <activity android:name=".ui.TransferMoneyActivity" android:exported="true"> with VIEW/DEFAULT/BROWSABLE + vulnbank://transfer; (3) <provider android:name=".data.AccountProvider" android:authorities="com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider" android:exported="true" />. All three set android:exported explicitly (true in every case); none carries an android:permission attribute; no custom <permission> is defined anywhere to apply even if desired.

reproduction_static: Full-manifest read confirms this is the complete component inventory -- no services, no receivers, no additional activities/providers exist in this file to also check.
reproduction_dynamic: If/when an installable build exists for this target, `adb shell dumpsys package com.vulnbankdemo.app` and/or drozer's `app.package.attacksurface` module would give a live-confirmed version of this same inventory (MAN-18).
notes: Logged per instructions to always provide the full exported-component inventory (even benign entries) for taint-flow-analyst and android-ipc-ui-auditor, since they need the complete surface map rather than just the two flagged findings. No further action needed on LoginActivity itself.
